name: Syndicalism
summary: Syndicalism is a revolutionary current of the labor movement that organizes workers by industry into unions and aims to end capitalism by direct action, culminating in a general strike. The unions are meant to be both the weapon of struggle and the embryo of the future society, running production themselves and making the state superfluous. It rejects parliamentary politics and party leadership, and is internationalist and anti-militarist.
scope: Classical revolutionary syndicalism as practiced by the French CGT (Charter of Amiens, 1906; Pouget, Griffuelhes), with the IWW and Spain's CNT as related organizations. It excludes Sorel's mythic-violence variant and the nationalist national-syndicalism, and does not separately treat the anarcho-syndicalist strand, which has its own entry.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The aim is social ownership and workers' control of production for the common good, not market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Syndicalists want industry run by union federations, not by the state, so state ownership is rejected as a model.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are both the weapon of struggle and the embryo of the new society.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Charter's long-term aim is the expropriation of the capitalists.

worker-ownership.rationale: Social ownership and workers' control of production is the central aim.

strong-leader.rationale: Pouget rejects representatives who stand between workers and their own power.

state-harmful.rationale: Syndicalists held the state to be the ruling class's tool, to be superseded by union organization, though some strands kept subsidiary territorial bodies.

empower-police-military.rationale: The army is seen as an obstacle and anti-militarism was a core method.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Patriotism was held to distract workers from class interests.

gradual-change.rationale: Syndicalists seek revolution culminating in a general strike, not gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The IWW welcomed immigrants and the CGT held that workers have no fatherland.

free-trade.rationale: Capitalist economic policy is opposed; not directly addressed.

nation-first.rationale: The CGT echoed the view that workers have no fatherland.

open-borders.rationale: Syndicalists were internationalist and held that workers have no fatherland.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Syndicalists accepted industrial progress and centralized large-scale industry.

revolution-justified.rationale: Syndicalism is a revolutionary current aiming at social revolution through the general strike.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cornelissen expected money and wages to persist while others wanted distribution by labor; adherents split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Production would be managed by workers through unions, not directed by the state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The aim is social ownership rather than distributed private property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Charter aims at the riddance of wage labor, though some syndicalists expected money to persist.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Charter demands union independence from the state and parties; state-recognized bodies contradict it.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Charter requires complete independence from political parties and the state.

democracy-best.rationale: Pouget calls parliamentarism false, and some syndicalists favored a revolutionary minority over the democracy of numbers.

direct-votes.rationale: Pouget rejects voting and referendums as substitutes for revolutionary action.

workers-councils.rationale: Unions and their federations would be the organs of the new society, which parallels councils.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pouget says force lies at the back of every movement and sabotage was endorsed.

war-builds-character.rationale: Anti-militarism and general strikes against war were core methods.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Syndicalists were internationalist and held that workers have no fatherland.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Syndicalists hold that society is divided into classes in constant struggle, following Marx; the "main driver of history" is not explicit.

civilizational-union.rationale: Internationalism of workers rejects identity-based political unions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Syndicalists accepted industrial progress and built on large-scale industry.

direct-action.rationale: Pouget calls direct action the emblem of revolutionary unionism, in preference to electoral politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: The IWW Preamble speaks of building the new society within the shell of the old, and Pouget refuses to sacrifice the present to the future.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Syndicalism organizes production by industry and accepts large-scale industry.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Pataud and Pouget kept distribution according to labor.

production-for-use.rationale: Unions would run industry for the common good.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The IWW Preamble says workers and employers have nothing in common, taking the Marxist view of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Syndicalists reject party and state rule; unions would run society, though some favored a revolutionary minority.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Syndicalists were anti-militarist and organized general strikes against war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Syndicalists are socialists who accept collective provision; the claim is a libertarian one.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The IWW welcomed all workers regardless of race.

organic-representation.rationale: Unions would replace parties as the basis of social organization, but families and communities are not mentioned.

total-state.rationale: The Charter demands independence from the state and syndicalists want it superseded.

bound-labor.rationale: The Charter aims at the riddance of wage labor, so bound labor is rejected a fortiori.

single-common-good.rationale: Syndicalists see classes as opposed with irreconcilable interests.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Production under workers' control is the core aim.

rule-by-example.rationale: Pouget rejects reliance on rulers and authority.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The IWW organized immigrants and the CGT held that workers have no fatherland.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Charter explicitly recognizes class struggle and rejects partnership with employers.

workers-nation.rationale: The CGT's 1908 congress held that workers have no fatherland.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The IWW organized workers of all races in one union.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Syndicalists accepted Marx's view of the state as the ruling class's executive committee.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary representation of any kind is rejected as a substitute for direct action.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

reviewHistory.rationale: Pouget calls parliamentary politics false and hypocritical.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The aim is social ownership and workers' control, not a limited state.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Syndicalists were internationalist, but the claim is not directly addressed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Syndicalists aim to replace the state with workers' organizations.

population-transfer.rationale: The IWW organized immigrants and rejected national exclusion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pouget says force is unavoidable and sabotage was endorsed.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Charter of Amiens makes the union independent of parties, and syndicalists hold that workers emancipate themselves through their own unions, not through a leading party.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The general strike and direct action are the central syndicalist weapon, and the Charter of Amiens keeps unions independent of the state.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The IWW organizes all workers regardless of origin and syndicalism is internationalist, so a cohesion-by-sameness claim is rejected.

party-controls-media.rationale: Unions are held independent of parties and the state, and syndicalism rejects state and party direction of workers.

party-commands-army.rationale: Syndicalism is anti-militarist and rejects the state and party leadership, so party command of the army is opposed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Syndicalism aims to make the state superfluous and is anti-militarist, so a ruler commanding the military is opposed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Syndicalism is secular and opposed to rule by any ruling class, including clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Syndicalism is anti-militarist and internationalist, but in 1914 the French CGT joined the union sacrée and took part in the war effort, while the IWW stayed anti-war without campaigning against it (s1); revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist idea, so the movement is split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist and anti-militarist, opposing wars and alliances among states that workers would fight.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Pouget stresses workers' own education against the stultifying schooling of the bourgeoisie, but the movement is not hostile to educated people as such.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Syndicalists oppose state authority and want workers' self-organization from below, so suspending freedoms for state-led development contradicts their principles.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Syndicalism rejects the state and parliamentary politics, so a state figurehead has no role.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Syndicalism is secular and class-based and rejects rulers' authority.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Syndicalism rejects state rule, and an unbound sovereign contradicts it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Syndicalism rejects parliaments and rule by an elite in favour of union self-management.

leader-cult.rationale: Syndicalism rejects party leadership and authority from above.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist and class-based, and rejects nationalist claims on territory.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Parliamentary majorities and state courts are both rejected as institutions; adherents would not defend either, so split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement is internationalist and anti-militarist and rejects autarkic national blocs.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Syndicalists expect revolution from mass organised workers through the general strike, not a small armed vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolition of classes and privilege is central, as in the IWW Preamble's end of the wage system and class divisions.

patriotic-education.rationale: Syndicalists were anti-militarist and held that workers have no fatherland, so teaching national loyalty and pride is rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The IWW organised all workers regardless of race or trade and held that an injury to one is an injury to all, so discrimination is rejected.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Syndicalism rejects parliamentary politics in favour of direct action and union self-rule, with the unions replacing the state.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The union is built on active participation in class struggle and in running production.

native-born-offices.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist, and class solidarity cuts across nationality.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Internationalist and anti-militarist, so adherents oppose wars and claims over territory.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Syndicalism is anti-militarist and opposes the army as an instrument of the ruling class.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about community or state ownership of land, and the statement now asks only whether a right to hold land should end when the holder stops using it.

reviewHistory.rationale: They want production and resources held by the unions on behalf of the community; not specifically addressed for land.

corporate-influence.rationale: Syndicalists see the capitalist class as owning the state and its politicians, so corporate sway over government is what they expect.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-militarist internationalists opposed imperial wars and intervention by states, though solidarity strikes across borders were welcomed.

industrial-unions.rationale: Organising by industry into one big union is the defining syndicalist form, as in the CGT federations and the IWW.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Their analysis is of class conflict, not ethnic plots, and internationalism rejects nationalist scapegoating.

informal-organisation.rationale: Syndicalism relies on permanent mass unions and federations, not small informal groups, which is a point of difference with insurrectionary anarchism.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject the state and nationalism, so national law taking precedence over international solidarity or law has no appeal.

religious-nation.rationale: Workers have no fatherland, and unions organise across religions, so a religiously defined nation is rejected.

majority-settlement.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist and opposes state-led national assimilation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Syndicalists reject both capitalism and parliamentary or party-led socialism in favour of union-run production; read loosely as a third course.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is the practice of the state and dictatorship that the ideology rejects, and it criticised the Bolsheviks for exactly this.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents are anti-clerical and oppose any state enforcing religion; punishing blasphemy would be authority at its worst.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism and internationalism follow from rejecting exploitation and the state; colonial rule for the ruler's benefit is exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct self-management by those affected, in workplaces and communities through federated assemblies, is the core of the ideology's alternative to the state.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The ideology sits firmly on the revolutionary left and sees capitalists and workers as opposed classes whose best ideas cannot be merged.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wage labour is condemned as wage slavery that cuts workers off from the product and control of their work, and free creative work is the aim.

social-market-economy.rationale: Both markets and wage relations are rejected, and the state-regulated compromise is rejected as well; production and distribution are to be organised in common.

rich-first.rationale: Equality and abolition of class privilege are central; letting some get rich first contradicts them.

property-franchise.rationale: Syndicalists reject parliamentary politics and class privilege, and the movement was built by propertyless workers, so a property vote is opposed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Syndicalism focuses on class and the workplace, and the sources do not link women's and nature's domination; adherents' views vary.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Syndicalists hold that workers lack real power while employers own the means of production, including the press, and they ran their own union papers.

racial-franchise.rationale: Syndicalism organises workers across industry and nation, as the IWW did across race, so it opposes ethnic limits on rights.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Solidarity across the working class is a core syndicalist value, so boycotting a religious minority's shops contradicts it, even though boycotts are used against employers.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Syndicalism is anti-militarist and internationalist and rejects state-run national organisation, so drilled youth for national service is rejected.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The IWW Preamble abolishes the wage system and holds that the working class produces the wealth, so returns on mere ownership are unearned.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pouget defends direct action including force and the general strike, so absolute pacifism is not the syndicalist view.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist and treats nations as secondary to class, so a continuous national essence is rejected.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Internationalism and anti-militarism reject sacralising death for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Syndicalists treat politics as class struggle over material interests and keep religion out of union affairs.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The IWW organised all workers regardless of nationality and race, rejecting economic roles tied to national groups.

independent-unions.rationale: The Charter of Amiens reaffirms the union's complete independence from parties and the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Syndicalists want the unions themselves to run production and replace the state, so a society run from above would not count as socialist.

municipal-property.rationale: Syndicalist production belongs to industrial unions and their federations, not to the town or the state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The syndicalist union federations coordinate local unions and labour exchanges from below, though organised by industry as well as place.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The IWW organises all workers regardless of race and syndicalism organises on class lines, not racial ones.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Syndicalism is class-based and internationalist, and the sources reject patriotism, so a nation of shared language over borders is not a unit it endorses.

communal-electorates.rationale: Syndicalists reject parliaments and electoral politics for direct action and are secular, so separate religious electorates are opposed.

arms-reduction.rationale: Revolutionary syndicalists oppose militarism and war between workers of different states, so reducing arms agrees in direction.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The CGT and IWW were strongly anti-militarist and called for strikes and refusal against war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Syndicalists organise workers collectively and press immediate demands, though they prefer direct action to contracts and aim at ending the wage system.

sacred-nation.rationale: Classical syndicalism is internationalist, class-based and secular, in contrast to national-syndicalism, which the scope excludes.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Charter of Amiens keeps the union fully independent of parties, so workers organise through unions rather than a party seeking office.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Classical syndicalism did not address this tradeoff, and adherents would be split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Pouget rejects parliaments as a screen for class rule and puts real power in direct action and union self-government, so elections alone do not suffice.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Syndicalists want the means of production held and run by the unions, rejecting private ownership by first claim.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist and anti-militarist, loyal to class rather than nation, though it does not discuss a spiritual tie to land directly.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Syndicalists reject parties and leaders but build their politics through industrial unions, so a leader bypassing groups is opposed.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The IWW preamble and Pouget hold that workers create wealth and the owning class lives off it, which is the core of the syndicalist case against capital.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Syndicalism is internationalist and anti-militarist, treating patriotism as a divide among workers.

missingStatements.text: A general strike is the best way to bring down capitalism.
missingStatements.rationale: The general strike is the final step to revolution, which Griffuelhes called the curtain drop on a tired old scene, and Pouget calls it direct action at its ultimate.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions should remain independent of all political parties.
missingStatements.rationale: The Charter of Amiens reaffirms the union's complete independence from parties and the state.

notes: The French CGT practice was more ambiguous than the doctrine on parliamentary politics. Distribution in the future society was disputed: some wanted distribution by labor, others expected wages and money to persist. Sorel's violence myth is not part of the profile.
